create.name: Charles Freligh
create.bio:
Charles Freligh is a meditation teacher, writer and retreat leader based in Northfield, Minnesota. He trained as a clinical psychologist and earned a doctorate in the field, and he also teaches at university level and makes visual art. A period spent living at a Zen monastery in upstate New York shaped much of his practice, though he does not call himself a Buddhist. He draws freely on Zen, Taoism and Western philosophy, treating the world's traditions as different ways of pointing at the same simple experience of being here.

His teaching is plain and unhurried, centred on presence, stillness and letting life unfold without forcing it. He offers one-to-one guidance online, which he sees as neither coaching nor therapy, and leads small group retreats each year: a mindfulness retreat in the hills of Los Altos, California, a Tao weekend near Minneapolis and a Zen retreat at Dai Bosatsu Zendo in the Catskills. His book The Will to Do Nothing explores why stillness matters in a busy life. On Insight Timer he shares guided meditations, Zen stories and short courses on the Tao Te Ching, and his YouTube channel holds brief lessons on the basics of mindfulness practice.

books.title: The Will to Do Nothing: An Expression of the Heart
books.author: Charles Freligh
books.description: Charles's book on stillness and the quiet art of not doing, mixing personal stories with ideas from psychology, meditation research and contemplative traditions. It makes a case for slowing down and simply being present as a way of living more fully.

courses.title: Individual Guidance
courses.description: One-to-one online meetings with Charles focused on being more present in everyday life and on what gets in the way of that. A 30-minute first meeting ($50 USD) checks the fit before regular 50-minute sessions; he notes a short waiting list.

courses.title: Here and Now 2027: A Mindfulness Retreat
courses.description: A four-day residential mindfulness retreat at El Retiro Jesuit Retreat Center in the hills above Los Altos, California. Days mix guided and silent sitting, mindful listening and optional gentle movement, with unscheduled time for rest and walks.

courses.title: Wu Wei Weekend 2027: A Tao Retreat
courses.description: A small residential retreat at Mount Olivet Retreat Center south of Minneapolis, built around the Taoist idea of effortless action. Group meditation and discussion inspired by the Tao Te Ching sit alongside walks, yoga and time for creative work.
courses.price: $1950 USD; $3400 USD for a couple sharing a room

courses.title: The Zen Path 2027: A Pilgrimage to Now
courses.description: A retreat at Dai Bosatsu Zendo, a Rinzai Zen monastery on Beecher Lake in the Catskill Mountains, with up to four hours of zazen a day, long stretches of silence and twice-daily talks. It uses traditional Zen forms without being a formal Buddhist retreat.

courses.title: Zen Stories: 10 Gates Of Awakening
courses.description: A ten-day Insight Timer course of short Zen tales, some old and some from Charles's own time at a New York monastery. Each few-minute session invites a felt taste of the story rather than analysis.
courses.price: Included in Member Plus ($59.99 USD a year)

courses.title: The Tao In 10 Days
courses.description: A beginner-friendly Insight Timer course on the Tao Te Ching, taking a theme a day across ten sessions of around twelve minutes. Themes include yielding, non-judgement and acting without strain.
courses.price: Included in Member Plus ($59.99 USD a year)

free_resources.title: Charles Freligh on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Charles's free guided meditations and reflective talks, many drawing on Zen and the Tao, alongside his short courses. Free to listen in the app or on the web.

Email connect@charlesfreligh.com appears as a mailto link on the Wu Wei Weekend and At-Home Retreat pages (not on the contact page, which has a form); retreat questions also go to an organiser's personal Gmail, not used.
Retreat pages are dated 2027 but some internal lines still mention 2026 balance-due dates (e.g. 8/10/26, 5/3/26); dates taken from the headline 2027 dates.
He holds a clinical psychology PhD and Insight Timer calls him a remote therapist; his site frames the one-to-one work as non-clinical guidance and names no conditions, so kept.
Amazon's blurb for his book mentions his own struggles with anxiety; title and my description name no condition, so the book was kept.
YouTube view counts could not be read from the channel page (localised markup); videos chosen by topic, all short (2-6 min) teaching clips.
